Subject: Production — sustained 5xx spike + latency (urgent)

Sofia / Marissa,

We started seeing a sustained throughput spike on Friday morning (approx 07:40 PDT) that correlated with a rise in 5xx errors and downstream latency for a subset of our storefront endpoints. Error rate peaked at ~18% for 10 minutes and remained elevated (~4-6%) for ~70 minutes. Impact: pages timing out and queued jobs backing up.

We've restarted our app nodes and pushed attempted mitigations on our side but are still seeing errors tied to Redwood calls (tokenization/generation). Can you confirm whether there were any model switches, config changes, or capacity events on your side? We need a triage readout and ETA for mitigation steps — Sentinel is heading into a marketing push Monday and this is high priority.

Jordan
Head of Platform, Sentinel Retail

Subject: Re: Production — sustained 5xx spike + latency (urgent)

Jordan — immediate update from triage:
- Cause (preliminary): a misrouted batch of high-concurrency requests (long-context product indexing jobs) knocked an internal routing table into a fallback path that invoked a larger model variant without the expected batching profile. That combination drove synchronous KV-cache pressure and increased tokenization/encoder latency.
- Observable: CPU/GPU contention on two serving hosts and a cascading backlog in our request-queueing layer.
- Actions taken (completed): 1) Throttled the mistaken job at the ingress layer; 2) Forced the requests onto the intended model variant (smaller quantized model) and re-enabled prefetched KV caches; 3) Brought up two warm standby workers with adjusted batch sizing.
- Current state: error rate has reduced to ~0.8% and latency back within SLO for 15+ minutes. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours.

Planned follow-ups in next 24 hours:
- Permanent routing rule to prevent model-auto-fallback on that path (owner: Marissa, ETA: 2028-08-06 17:00 PDT)
- Autoscaling policy tweak to consider rapid short-lived spikes (owner: Karthik, ETA: 2028-08-07 12:00 PDT)
- Retro/RCA write-up and customer-facing remediation note (owner: Sofia, ETA: 2028-08-09 17:00 PDT)

We will share the RCA and an action tracker shortly. Apologies for the disruption — please escalate to your leadership if you're not seeing recovery in the next 30m.

Marissa
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Sentinel incident — RCA, remediation commitments, and closure

Jordan — attaching our formal RCA and the action tracker. Thank you for patience while we completed the analysis. Summary (customer-facing):
- Incident window: 2028-08-03T07:40:00-07:00 through 2028-08-03T09:00:00-07:00.
- Root cause: a chain of events where an unusually large batch from a long-context indexing job was routed to an auto-fallback model variant. The fallback path did not have the expected batching profile and caused synchronous KV-cache pressure, which cascaded into slower tokenization and a brief backlog on two serving hosts.
- Immediate mitigations taken: ingress throttling of the offending job, forced routing to the intended smaller quantized model, manual warm-worker spin-up, and cache prefill re-enablement.
- Preventative commitments and owners:
  * Disable auto-fallback for indexing-job route (owner: Marissa Cole) — ETA 2028-08-06 17:00 PDT (completed)
  * Autoscaler policy change to treat short spikes as transient (owner: Karthik Iyer) — ETA 2028-08-07 12:00 PDT (completed)
  * Add alerting and a small query-rate breaker at the ingress for long-context jobs (owner: Marissa Cole) — ETA 2028-08-14 12:00 PDT
  * Post-change perf validation and runbook updates (owner: Sofia Ivanova) — ETA 2028-08-16 17:00 PDT

Compensation: Grace is prepared to discuss a pro-rated credit if Sentinel elects to pursue that path; we'll keep that conversation separate from technical closure unless you ask for an executive readout.
